newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares get early boost from Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares get early boost from Wall Street.

text.p: Singapore shares, especially property counters, were firmer at mid-morning on Tuesday, boosted by a stronger overnight Wall Street, dealers said.
Property heavyweights like City Developments, DBS Land, Keppel Land and Wing Tai recovered from recent losses and were among the actives.
Dealers were sceptical the firmer property prices signalled a recovery following a Singapore government announcement on Saturday of loan curbs to public housing buyers.
"There is still concern of more curbs on public housing that might impact the private property markets," a dealer said.
"Prices of property counters are up...on Wall Street and some bargain-hunting" but buying was very restrained, the dealer said.
At 0215 GMT, the property index was up 7.75 points at 682.88. The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 5.86 points at 2,040.50. Turnover was light, with 150 gainers to 26 losers.
Multimedia company Creative Technology led gainers, rising Singapore $1.20 to S$17.90. Malaysia's North Borneo Timbers Bhd rose S$0.50 to S$11.40 on news it won a logging concession in Sabah.
Neptune Orient lines, which resumed trading on Tuesday after announcing a takeover bid for U.S.-based APL, was up 11 cents to S$1.33.
